name: whoami
description: Identify the authenticated user in Sentry. Use this tool when you need to know who the current user is.

name: find_organizations
description: Find organizations that the user has access to in Sentry. Use this tool when you need to view all organizations in Sentry or find an organization's slug.

query.description: Search query to filter results by name or slug.

name: find_teams
description: Find teams in an organization in Sentry. Use this tool when you need to view teams in a Sentry organization or find a team's slug.

query.description: Search query to filter results by name or slug.

name: find_projects
description: Find projects in Sentry. Use this tool when you need to view projects in a Sentry organization or find a project's slug.

query.description: Search query to filter results by name or slug.

name: find_releases
description: Find releases in Sentry. Use this tool when you need to find the most recent releases or information about a specific release version.

query.description: Search for versions which contain the provided string.

name: find_tags
description: Find tags in Sentry. Use this tool when you need to see which tags are available for filtering errors and events.

name: find_dsns
description: List all Sentry DSNs for a specific project. Use this tool when you need to retrieve a DSN for configuring an SDK.

name: get_issue_details
description: Get detailed information about a specific Sentry issue by ID, including the stacktrace of the latest event. Use this tool when you need to investigate an error or exception reported in Sentry.

eventId.description: The ID of a specific event.

name: get_event_attachment
description: Download attachments from a Sentry event, such as minidumps, screenshots, or log files.

attachmentId.description: The ID of the attachment to download.

name: update_issue
description: Update an issue's status or assignment in Sentry. Use this tool to resolve, ignore, or unresolve an issue, or to assign it to a user or team.

status.description: The new status: resolved, resolvedInNextRelease, unresolved, or ignored.

name: search_events
description: Search for events in Sentry using natural language, and get counts and aggregations. Use this tool for error counts, performance metrics, and spans, e.g. 'how many errors today' or 'slowest API calls'.

naturalLanguageQuery.description: Natural language description of the events to search for.

projectSlug.description: Optional project to scope the search.

name: search_issues
description: Search for grouped issues in Sentry using natural language. Returns a list of issues with basic information, e.g. 'unresolved errors from the last day' or 'critical bugs assigned to me'.

naturalLanguageQuery.description: Natural language description of the issues to search for.

projectSlugOrId.description: Optional project to scope the search.

name: create_team
description: Create a new team in Sentry.

name.description: The name of the team to create.

name: create_project
description: Create a new project in Sentry, giving you access to a new SDK client key (DSN).

name.description: The name of the project to create.

platform.description: The platform for the project, e.g. python or javascript.

name: update_project
description: Update project settings in Sentry, such as its name, slug, platform, or team assignment.

name.description: The new name for the project.

name: create_dsn
description: Create an additional DSN for an existing project.

name.description: The name of the DSN to create.

name: analyze_issue_with_seer
description: Use Seer to analyze a production error and get a root cause analysis with a specific code fix recommendation.

instruction.description: Optional custom instruction for the analysis.

name: search_docs
description: Search Sentry documentation for SDK setup, instrumentation, and configuration guidance.

query.description: The search query in natural language.

name: get_doc
description: Fetch the full markdown content of a Sentry documentation page.

path.description: The documentation path, from search_docs results.
